title: Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana: RSBY Card Status 2026
meta_description: Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY) gave BPL families Rs 30,000 health cover. It merged into Ayushman Bharat PMJAY in 2018. Check eligibility at pmjay.gov.in.

hero.one_liner: Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY) gave BPL families Rs 30,000 health cover. It merged into Ayushman Bharat in 2018. What old cardholders should do now.

what_is_it: Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY) was India's first national health insurance scheme for below-poverty-line (BPL) families, launched in 2008 by the UPA government under the Ministry of Labour and Employment. The scheme marked a landmark shift in Indian health policy, making cashless hospitalisation accessible to millions of unorganised sector workers and BPL households for the first time.

RSBY gave each enrolled family of up to five members a health cover of Rs 30,000 per year on a floater basis, meaning the entire amount could be used by any combination of family members in that year. The coverage included secondary hospitalisation, pre-existing diseases from day one, and transport assistance of Rs 100 per visit with an annual cap of Rs 1,000.

how_to_apply.title: Check if you are now covered under Ayushman Bharat PMJAY
how_to_apply.description: RSBY has been merged into Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY nationally since 2018. All former RSBY beneficiaries in states that have adopted Ayushman Bharat are now eligible for Rs 5 lakh annual health cover instead of the earlier Rs 30,000. Visit pmjay.gov.in and click on 'Am I Eligible' to check your household's current status using mobile number or ration card number.

how_to_apply.title: Get your Ayushman Bharat health card (Ayushman card)
how_to_apply.description: If your name appears in the Ayushman Bharat beneficiary list, visit the nearest Common Service Centre (CSC), empanelled hospital or government office with your Aadhaar card and ration card to apply for your Ayushman Bharat health card (ABHA-linked golden card). The card is issued free of cost. With it, you can access Rs 5 lakh cashless treatment at over 30,000 empanelled hospitals across India.

how_to_apply.title: West Bengal residents: check Swasthya Sathi status
how_to_apply.description: West Bengal did not implement Ayushman Bharat until May 2026. WB residents who were RSBY beneficiaries were migrated to the Swasthya Sathi scheme (Rs 5 lakh cover). Check your Swasthya Sathi card status at data.swasthyasathi.gov.in or call 18003455384. From mid-2026, Ayushman Bharat rollout in WB began and families can expect Ayushman Bharat cards from July 2026 onwards.

how_to_apply.title: For unorganised sector workers: check ESIC coverage
how_to_apply.description: Unorganised sector workers who were covered under RSBY may now be eligible for health coverage through ESIC (Employees' State Insurance Corporation) if their employer has registered them under the scheme. ESIC provides comprehensive health coverage including OPD, hospitalization, maternity and disability benefits. Check at esic.gov.in using your ESIC number.

how_to_apply.title: Look up the archived RSBY data if needed
how_to_apply.description: The original RSBY portal at rsby.gov.in is archived and is no longer accepting new applications. However, it may still contain beneficiary records that can be referenced for historical purposes or for proving prior RSBY enrollment when applying for Ayushman Bharat. Contact the nearest District Health Office if you need to access your RSBY beneficiary records.

ministry: Ministry of Labour (historical); now National Health Authority

extra_sections.title: RSBY Is Closed: Read This First
extra_sections.content:
Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana was merged into Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY in 2018 and is no longer active. Old RSBY smart cards are not accepted at hospitals.

If you were an RSBY beneficiary, check whether your family is now covered under Ayushman Bharat, which gives a much higher Rs 5 lakh cover.

extra_sections.heading: How RSBY Worked
content: The scheme was funded with a premium split of 75 percent from the Central government and 25 percent from the State government. States chose a public sector insurer or private insurer through competitive bidding to administer the scheme in their state, and the insurer managed hospital empanelment and claim processing.

Enrollment under RSBY was done through special camps organized in districts and blocks, where BPL beneficiaries gave their fingerprint biometric and had their photograph captured by the enrollment operator. Each family received a smart card based on the SCOSTA (Smart Card OS for Transport Applications) standard that could be used at any empanelled hospital across the country.

The RSBY smart card carried the details of up to five family members and worked at any empanelled RSBY hospital nationwide, giving it national portability. A family enrolled in Bihar could get treatment at an RSBY-empanelled hospital in Delhi, Gujarat or Maharashtra without any additional paperwork, which was a significant innovation for migrant worker families.

items.title: India's first national health cover
items.sub: Launched 2008 by the Labour Ministry, RSBY gave BPL families cashless secondary hospitalisation through a biometric smart card.

items.title: Rs 30,000 per family
items.sub: Each family of up to five members got Rs 30,000 a year on a family floater basis, with pre-existing diseases covered from day one.

items.title: 75:25 funding
items.sub: The premium was split 75 percent central and 25 percent state. Over 35 states implemented it, covering 3.6 crore families at its peak.

items.title: Biometric smart card
items.sub: The card worked at any empanelled hospital nationally, an early example of portable, paperless, cashless public health insurance.

extra_sections.heading: Coverage and Its Limits
content: Pre-existing diseases were covered from the very first day under RSBY, unlike many private health insurance products that imposed waiting periods of two to four years for pre-existing conditions. This feature made the scheme genuinely useful for the poor who typically suffer from chronic conditions rooted in poverty and limited nutrition.

RSBY's coverage of Rs 30,000 per family per year was, however, inadequate for most secondary and tertiary care procedures, especially as medical costs rose through the late 2000s and early 2010s. A single hospital admission for a heart condition or cancer treatment could exhaust the annual limit within one or two procedures.

All secondary hospitalisation procedures (requiring at least one night in hospital) that the state government listed in its RSBY package were covered. The standard package included over 700 procedures ranging from cataract surgery to hernia repair, appendectomy, fracture treatment, dialysis and childbirth-related complications.

extra_sections.title: What Replaced the Old Rs 30,000
extra_sections.desc:
Ayushman Bharat raised the cover from RSBY's Rs 30,000 to Rs 5 lakh per family per year.

It also covers far more procedures and has national portability, so eligible families get cashless treatment at empanelled hospitals across India.

extra_sections.heading: Why RSBY Merged Into Ayushman Bharat
content: In 2018, the Modi government launched Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY), a new health insurance scheme with Rs 5 lakh cover per family per year. RSBY was formally merged into Ayushman Bharat, and all RSBY beneficiaries were automatically upgraded to PM-JAY eligibility with the significantly higher coverage amount.

The merger of RSBY into Ayushman Bharat meant that RSBY cardholders did not need to re-register from scratch. States transitioned existing RSBY data into the PM-JAY beneficiary database, and new Ayushman Bharat health cards (popularly called the golden card) were issued in place of RSBY smart cards at Common Service Centres and government offices.

RSBY empanelled hospitals had to install biometric readers and IT infrastructure at the front desk to authenticate beneficiaries using the smart card and fingerprint reader. This technology-first approach reduced fraud, as each admission was authenticated in real time against the central RSBY server rather than relying on paper records.

rows: Active across all states except partial WB transition

extra_sections.heading: What Changed for Beneficiaries
content: Ayushman Bharat health cards are issued in the name of each family member individually, unlike RSBY which issued one family smart card, with each person getting their own ABHA (Ayushman Bharat Health Account) card linked to Aadhaar. This ABHA card serves both as a health insurance identity and as a digital health record holder, a significant improvement over the RSBY model.

The hospital network under Ayushman Bharat is substantially larger than the RSBY hospital list. While RSBY had around 10,000 to 12,000 empanelled hospitals at its peak, Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY has over 30,000 empanelled hospitals across India including public sector hospitals in every state, private hospitals, and hospitals run by trusts and charities.

Hospitals submitted claims electronically through the RSBY IT platform and were paid within defined timelines. The scheme had a district-level monitoring unit and insurance company field staff who conducted physical audits of empanelled hospitals to verify admissions and prevent fraud.

extra_sections.heading: What You Should Do Now
content: For residents of states other than West Bengal, the question of RSBY coverage is now straightforward: RSBY no longer exists as a separate scheme and has been replaced by Ayushman Bharat PMJAY since 2018. Former RSBY beneficiaries should check their eligibility on pmjay.gov.in and obtain an Ayushman Bharat golden card if they have not already done so.

Families holding old RSBY smart cards should not use them at hospitals, as the scheme is closed and the backend server no longer validates RSBY transactions. They should obtain an Ayushman Bharat golden card (in most states) or a Swasthya Sathi card (in West Bengal) to continue accessing cashless hospital treatment.

More than 35 states and union territories eventually implemented RSBY, covering over 3.6 crore families at its peak. The scheme demonstrated that a large-scale technology-driven health insurance programme was operationally feasible in India, providing the institutional learning and IT architecture that later informed the design of Ayushman Bharat.

extra_sections.heading: What Former RSBY Cardholders Should Do

steps.title: Check Ayushman status
steps.desc: Visit beneficiary.nha.gov.in or call 14555 to see if your family is on the Ayushman Bharat list, as most RSBY families were migrated automatically.

steps.title: Get your Ayushman card
steps.desc: If eligible, generate your Ayushman card at a CSC, empanelled hospital, or via the portal. Cards are issued per individual, not per family.

steps.title: WB residents check Swasthya Sathi
steps.desc: In West Bengal, check Swasthya Sathi status, and watch for the 2026 Ayushman Bharat rollout in the state.

steps.title: Unorganised workers check ESIC
steps.desc: Workers registered through welfare boards should also check ESIC and state worker-welfare cover.

items.title: Much higher cover
items.sub: Rs 5 lakh versus Rs 30,000, covering tertiary care and high-value procedures RSBY could not afford.

items.title: Individual cards
items.sub: Ayushman cards are issued per family member, unlike RSBY's single family card for up to five members.

items.title: Bigger hospital network
items.sub: The empanelled network is far larger than RSBY's, run on the PM-JAY Beneficiary Identification System.

items.title: National portability
items.sub: Eligible families get cashless treatment at empanelled hospitals in any state, kept from RSBY's portable design.

extra_sections.heading: The West Bengal Case
content: West Bengal did not adopt Ayushman Bharat under the Mamata Banerjee government. RSBY in WB was superseded by the Swasthya Sathi scheme launched in December 2016, which provided Rs 5 lakh cashless cover with no central government funding, and former RSBY cardholders in WB were enrolled in Swasthya Sathi automatically.

In May 2026, after the BJP formed the West Bengal government following the state assembly election, the new cabinet approved the adoption of Ayushman Bharat PMJAY in WB. The transition is expected to bring WB RSBY and Swasthya Sathi beneficiaries fully into the national Ayushman Bharat network, giving them coverage at hospitals across India for the first time.

The Ayushman Bharat scheme is administered by the National Health Authority (NHA), and eligibility is determined by the Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) 2011 data for rural families and the National Urban Livelihoods Mission occupational criteria for urban families. Families who were RSBY beneficiaries may already be in the Ayushman Bharat beneficiary list based on SECC data.

extra_sections.title: The West Bengal Situation
extra_sections.content:
WB did not adopt Ayushman Bharat under the previous government and ran Swasthya Sathi instead, so RSBY beneficiaries there moved to Swasthya Sathi.

In May 2026 the new WB government approved Ayushman Bharat for the state, with rollout underway. WB residents should check both Swasthya Sathi and the new Ayushman cards.

extra_sections.heading: Unorganised Workers and Welfare Boards
content: Unorganised sector workers such as construction labourers, domestic workers, rickshaw pullers, street vendors, ragpickers, agricultural workers and beedi workers were the primary target group for RSBY. These groups are also prioritised under Ayushman Bharat and under various state health schemes, recognizing that formal employment-linked health insurance (ESIC) does not reach them.

Unorganised sector workers who were enrolled under RSBY through welfare board registrations (construction workers, beedi workers, etc.) are covered under Ayushman Bharat through a separate channel: the Building and Other Construction Workers (BOCW) welfare boards in their state. BOCW-registered workers should check with their state BOCW office to confirm their Ayushman Bharat enrollment.

Researchers and policy analysts often cite RSBY as both a partial success and a learning ground, as it enrolled tens of millions of families and paid billions of rupees in claims, demonstrating political will and implementation capacity. The coverage inadequacy at Rs 30,000, incomplete state participation and exclusion of the poorest households were the lessons that directly shaped Ayushman Bharat's design choices.

items.title: Confirm old enrolment
items.sub: District health officers in most states keep records of former RSBY beneficiaries and can help confirm 2008-2018 enrolment.

items.title: Use the NHA grievance system
items.sub: The National Health Authority runs a grievance portal and the 14555 helpline for Ayushman Bharat eligibility and card issues.

items.title: State health agency
items.sub: Each state's State Health Agency is the nodal body for Ayushman Bharat. Contact it for local enrolment and hospital queries.

items.title: Do not use old cards
items.sub: Old RSBY cards are not valid at hospitals. Carry your Ayushman card or check Swasthya Sathi in WB instead.

extra_sections.heading: Confirming Old RSBY Enrolment
content: District health officers in most states maintain a record of former RSBY beneficiaries and can assist families whose names may have been lost in the transition to Ayushman Bharat. Families who were enrolled in RSBY but do not find their names in the Ayushman Bharat list should approach the District Collector's office or the State Health Agency to request inclusion.

Individuals who need to confirm whether their family was enrolled in RSBY between 2008 and 2018 can approach the state insurance company that administered RSBY in their state during that period. Insurance companies that ran RSBY in various states include United India Insurance, New India Assurance, ICICI Lombard and Oriental Insurance, depending on the state and the bid cycle.

extra_sections.heading: RSBY's Legacy
content: The institutional legacy of RSBY extends beyond just beneficiary migration. The RSBY IT platform, biometric enrollment infrastructure, hospital empanelment methodology and claim processing architecture were all repurposed and scaled up to build the Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY system, making RSBY a foundational chapter in the history of universal health coverage in India.

The RSBY scheme, despite being superseded, represents an important milestone in India's journey toward universal health coverage. It proved that biometric smart card technology could work at population scale for a welfare scheme, demonstrated that cashless health coverage could reduce catastrophic health expenditure for poor families, and generated the institutional knowledge and IT frameworks that made Ayushman Bharat possible.

faqs.question: What is Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY)?
faqs.answer:
Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY) was India's national health insurance scheme for BPL families and unorganised sector workers, launched in 2008. It gave families of up to five members Rs 30,000 cashless health cover per year at empanelled hospitals.

RSBY was merged into Ayushman Bharat PMJAY in 2018 and is no longer active.

faqs.question: Is RSBY still active in 2026?
faqs.answer:
No. RSBY was merged into Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY) in 2018 and is no longer a separate scheme. Old RSBY cards are not accepted at hospitals.

Former RSBY beneficiaries should check their Ayushman Bharat eligibility at pmjay.gov.in.

faqs.question: What happened to RSBY beneficiaries after the scheme closed?
faqs.answer: In most states, RSBY beneficiaries were automatically migrated to Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY, which provides Rs 5 lakh cover per family per year instead of the earlier Rs 30,000. Beneficiaries need to get a new Ayushman Bharat golden card from a Common Service Centre, empanelled hospital or government office.

faqs.question: What was the RSBY coverage amount?
faqs.answer:
RSBY provided Rs 30,000 per family of up to five members per year on a floater basis for secondary hospitalisation. It also included transport assistance of Rs 100 per visit (maximum Rs 1,000 per year).

All pre-existing diseases were covered from day one.

faqs.question: How do I check my Ayushman Bharat eligibility as a former RSBY beneficiary?
faqs.answer:
Visit pmjay.gov.in and click on 'Am I Eligible'. Enter your mobile number (registered with the scheme) or ration card number to check if your family appears in the Ayushman Bharat beneficiary list.

If eligible, visit a CSC or empanelled hospital with your Aadhaar and ration card to get your Ayushman Bharat golden card free of cost.

faqs.question: What is the RSBY status in West Bengal?
faqs.answer:
In West Bengal, RSBY was replaced by the Swasthya Sathi scheme in December 2016 before the national RSBY-PMJAY merger. WB RSBY beneficiaries were migrated to Swasthya Sathi, which provides Rs 5 lakh cashless cover.

From mid-2026, WB is transitioning to Ayushman Bharat under the new BJP state government. Check swasthyasathi.gov.in or call 18003455384.

faqs.question: Can I still use my RSBY card at a hospital?
faqs.answer:
No. RSBY cards are no longer active at hospitals. The RSBY backend system is closed and hospital biometric terminals will reject old RSBY smart cards.

You should obtain an Ayushman Bharat health card (in most states) or a Swasthya Sathi card (if you are in West Bengal) to access cashless treatment.

faqs.question: What is the difference between RSBY and Ayushman Bharat?
faqs.answer:
RSBY (2008) gave Rs 30,000 cover to BPL families of up to 5 members. Ayushman Bharat (2018) gives Rs 5 lakh cover with no family size cap and national portability at 30,000+ hospitals across India.

AB-PMJAY also covers a much wider range of 1,900+ procedures and uses ABHA-linked digital health cards instead of SCOSTA smart cards.

faqs.question: What is the RSBY helpline number?
faqs.answer:
The original RSBY helpline is no longer active. For Ayushman Bharat queries, call the toll-free helpline 14555.

For West Bengal's Swasthya Sathi scheme, call 18003455384 (24x7 toll-free).

faqs.question: Who was eligible for RSBY?
faqs.answer: RSBY eligibility was based on the BPL list of the respective state. Unorganised sector workers including construction workers, beedi workers, domestic workers, rickshaw pullers, street vendors, ragpickers and mine workers were also covered under RSBY through their respective welfare boards, even if not in the BPL list.
